figures.caption: Figure 2: Compared with classic speculative decoding (shown in (a) rigid verification), our Diversed (c) achieves a higher acceptance rate, comparable accuracy, and lower wall-clock time. Compared with static ensemble (b), Diversed (c) attains higher accuracy via a tunable ensemble weight that adapts to the task and the context.

Figure 4: Normalized total time (lower is better) versus acceptance rate (higher is better) under speculative decoding with draft length N=5. Model pairs with higher acceptance achieve lower decoding time. Results on the CNNDM, XSUM, MBPP, and GSM8K datasets for three target/draft pairs. Additional results for draft lengths N=3 and N=7 are provided in Appendix Figures 8 and 9.

Table 1: Benchmark acceptance rate and generation quality. Columns group results by task while panels (a)–(c) correspond to different Target/Draft model pairs. All experiments use temperature 1 and draft length N = 5. Our Diversed achieves a higher acceptance rate and also maintains comparable quality. Additional results for temperatures 0 and 0.1 are reported in Appendix Tables 6 and 7.
Table 4: List of notations and their definitions.

Table 7: Reported acceptance rate and generation quality, under different temperature. Columns are grouped by task. Each block compares three baselines and our method for a given Target/Draft pair. All results use a temperature of 0.1 and a draft length N = 5. Our Diversed enjoys a higher acceptance rate and also maintains comparable quality to baselines.

Table 6: Reported acceptance rate and generation quality. Columns are grouped by task. Each block compares three baselines and our method for a given Target/Draft pair. All results use temperature 0 and draft length N = 5. Our Diversed enjoys a higher acceptance rate and also maintains comparable quality to baselines.

Figure 5: Diversed consistently accepts a larger average number of draft tokens per verification round than all baselines (draft length N=5, temperature 1). Appendix Figure 7 shows result for temperature 0.1.
Table 2: Comparison of finetuned draft vs. Diversed at temperature 1. Fine-tuned draft model yields higher acceptance rates but lower task performance.

Figure 3: Examples of speculative-decoding verification with accepted mismatches, illustrating not all draft– target mismatches are equally harmful. Black marks tokens both models agree on; green marks accepted mismatches that still yield the correct answer; red marks accepted mismatches that lead to an incorrect answer.

Figure 8: Results on the CNNDM, XSUM, MBPP, and GSM8k datasets for three target/draft pairs: normalized total time (lower is better) versus acceptance rate (higher is better) under speculative decoding with N=3. Model pairs with higher acceptance achieve lower decoding time.

Figure 7: Average number of tokens accepted per verification round (temperature = 0.1, draft length N = 5) across three target/draft model pairs. Our Diversed consistently surpasses all baselines by achieving a higher number of accepted tokens.

Figure 9: Results on the CNNDM, XSUM, MBPP, and GSM8k datasets for three target/draft pairs: normalized total time (lower is better) versus acceptance rate (higher is better) under speculative decoding with N=7. Model pairs with higher acceptance achieve lower decoding time.
Table 5: Hyper-parameter configuration for each benchmark dataset.

Figure 10: Our Diversed outperforms the Pareto front of the static ensemble and other baselines. Results are reported on the CNNDM dataset using the target/draft model pair: Qwen3-8B/Qwen3-0.6B and Gemma-3-12bit/Gemma-3-4b-it, with temperature set to 0.
